question: Should I Add an Express Checkout Button Above the Regular Payment Form?
metaDescription: Usually yes for mobile traffic specifically — express buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal) skip form-filling entirely and tend to lift conversion there.
shortAnswer: For most stores with meaningful mobile traffic, yes — express checkout buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal's one-click option) let a customer complete a purchase using details already stored in their device or account, skipping manual form-filling entirely. This tends to measurably improve mobile conversion specifically, where typing out card and address details is the most friction-heavy part of checkout.

image.alt: An express checkout button positioned above the standard payment form, letting mobile customers skip manual form-filling entirely

bodyHtml:
Why Express Buttons Help

Express checkout options pull shipping and payment details directly from the customer's device wallet or existing account, pre-filling everything a standard form would otherwise require typing manually. On mobile in particular, where typing is slower and more error-prone than on desktop, this shortcut removes the single biggest source of checkout friction — which is why express buttons consistently show a meaningful conversion lift specifically on mobile traffic in most stores that test them.

Getting the Placement and Setup Right

  • Position matters — express buttons are typically most effective placed prominently above the regular payment form (or even on the cart page), rather than buried below it where a customer has already started manually filling in details.
  • Not every customer has an eligible wallet set up, so the regular payment form still needs to work well as a fallback — express checkout is an addition, not a replacement.
  • Multiple express options together (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal) cover different customer device/account combinations, and offering more than one tends to be better than picking just one, within reason.
  • Domain verification and HTTPS requirements apply to Apple Pay and Google Pay specifically, the same prerequisites relevant to those buttons showing up at all elsewhere in checkout.

Setting It Up

  1. Confirm the active gateway supports express checkout buttons and complete any required domain verification.
  2. Position the buttons prominently — near the top of checkout, and consider the cart page too if the gateway supports it there.
  3. Test on real mobile devices with actual wallet accounts set up, since a desktop-only test won't reveal the full experience.
  4. Monitor mobile conversion before and after to confirm the expected lift for the specific store's audience.
